th Order No. 04/Dated 11 December, 2024 I.A. No.12831 of 2024 1.

This interlocutory application has been filed for suspension of sentence in connection with order of sentence dated 08.09.2023 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-1-cum-Special Judge (POCSO Act), Koderma in Special POCSO Case No.09 of 2022 arising out of Jainagar P.S. Case No.37 of 2022, by which the appellant has been sentenced and directed to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 25 years with fine of Rs.30,000/- under Section 376-AB of the I.P.C. and in default of payment of fine, further S.I. for two years.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-1-cum-Special Judge (POCSO Act), Koderma
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. It has been contended on behalf of the appellant that it is a case where the testimony as has been given by the victim, who has been examined as PW-10, is not being corroborated from the medical evidence.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant has further submitted that the other witnesses have not corroborated the prosecution version, as such, it is a fit case where the sentence is to be suspended.
4. While on the other hand, Mr. Pankaj Kumar Mishra, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the State, has vehemently opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence.

sentences.text: It has been contended that it is a case where five years' old female child has been subjected to sexual assault that too by the neighbor and that is the reason the conviction is under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.

6. It has been submitted that considering the age of the victim and her testimony having been corroborated by her supported by the testimony of PW-1, the mother and PW-2, the grandmother,
the evidence of the Doctor is immaterial.
Therefore, the submission has been made that it is a case where the sentence is not to be suspended considering the nature of the crime committed by the appellant.

7. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the finding recorded by the learned trial court in the impugned judgment as also the testimony available in the L.C.R. and the exhibits as available therein.
8. It is a case where the five years' female child has been subjected to sexual assault.
She has supported the prosecution version having been examined as PW-10.
PW-1 the mother of the victim and PW-9 the grandmother of the victim have also supported the prosecution version.

Even the victim has supported the prosecution version in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
and remained consistent by corroborated the prosecution version.
9. In view of the aforesaid, in such nature of case the evidence of the Doctor has become immaterial.
10. Regard being had to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that the instant interlocutory application is fit to be rejected.
11. Accordingly, the prayer for suspension of sentence of the appellant is rejected.
12. Accordingly, I.A. No. 12831 of 2024, is hereby dismissed.
13. However, it is made clear that any observation made herein will not prejudice the case on merit as the appeal is lying pending for its consideration.

(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) (Navneet Kumar, J.) Birendra/
